questions.knowledge_point: Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
questions.problem: Find the solution to the equation ${e}^{1-2x}=5$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take $ln$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{1-2x} & =5 \\ ln⁡({e}^{1-2x}) & =ln⁡(5) \\ 1-2x & =ln⁡(5) \\ -2x & =ln⁡(5)-1 \\ x & =\frac{1-ln⁡(5)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
x≈-0.305
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1}-1 & =3 \\ {e}^{y+1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1} & =4 \\ ln⁡({e}^{y+1}) & =ln⁡(4) \\ y+1 & =2ln⁡(2) \\ y & =2ln⁡(2)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=2ln⁡(2)-1.$

questions.problem: If ${e}^{x+2}-7=2,$ then $x≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2}-7 & =2 \\ {e}^{x+2} & =2+7 \\ {e}^{x+2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2} & =9 \\ ln⁡({e}^{x+2}) & =ln⁡(9) \\ x+2 & =ln⁡(9) \\ x & =ln⁡(9)-2\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
x≈0.197
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.problem: If ${e}^{5+y/2}-9=21,$ then $y≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{5+y/2}-9 & =21 \\ {e}^{5+y/2} & =21+9 \\ {e}^{5+y/2} & =30\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{5+y/2} & =30 \\ ln⁡({e}^{5+y/2}) & =ln⁡(30) \\ 5+\frac{y}{2} & =ln⁡(30) \\ \frac{y}{2} & =ln⁡(30)-5 \\ y & =2ln⁡(30)-10\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
y≈-3.198
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
